raw_products.bookDescription:
Color the birds you already know — and a few you'll want to meet next.Backyard Birds brings 45 of North America's most-loved feathered neighbors to the page — from the unmistakable Northern Cardinal and Blue Jay to chickadees, goldfinches, woodpeckers, and more. Every bird is drawn true to life and clearly named, so each page is a small moment of discovery as much as a chance to slow down.
These are bold & easy designs, made the way coloring should feel. Each bird is rendered in clean, simple lines that are a pleasure to fill in, set against a richly detailed natural background — approachable enough for a complete beginner, satisfying enough for a seasoned colorist. No frustration, just calm, rewarding pages.
Thoughtful details you'll appreciate: every design is printed single-sided, so your finished work never bleeds or shows through, and the pages take colored pencils, markers, and gel pens beautifully.
Whether you're a lifelong birdwatcher, a backyard feeder-watcher, or simply someone who unwinds with a little color at the end of the day, this book was made for you.
A gift that always lands. For the bird lover, the nature enthusiast, the grandparent who has everything, or the friend who needs an excuse to relax — and just as perfect to keep for yourself. Ideal for birthdays, holidays, Mother's Day, and Father's Day.
Backyard Birds is part of the Field & Feather collection — coloring books for everyone who finds a little joy in the natural world, one page at a time.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Absolutely beautiful pictures difficult to color in tightly bound bookAbsolutely beautiful pictures difficult to color in tightly bound book
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So let me start with the positives. This book is tightly bound in a beautiful cover. The illustrations are absolutely gorgeous almost too pretty to color in. If you wanted muted tones of grays you could just frame these pictures the way that they are. Now for the negatives of which there are only two. The first being that your ink will bleed through onto the next page if you don't either cut the page out or protect it with a piece of cardboard underneath which of course will ruin your next picture. The second drawback is that because the book is so tightly bound it makes it really really difficult to color these pages inside the book. The pages are not perforated so you cannot just tear them out. Trying to cut them out is also difficult because the spine is so tight. So as you work your way further into the book it becomes harder and harder to color while they are connected to the spine. Overall this is a beautiful book with beautiful illustrations. I've colored my first page and am thrilled with the outcome. But it was also the first page so it wasn't difficult to comfortably color while attached. I'm not sure if the company would be willing to put their illustrations in a spiral book which would be so much better or just provide perforated pages. Either would be a huge improvement on a beautiful book. I can recommend this as a purchase just be aware of those two drawbacks.

raw_products.bookDescription:
Title: Colorado Birdwatching Coloring Book – A Cozy Coloring Adventure with 30 Backyard Birds – Track, Discover, and RelaxSeries: 50-State Birdwatching Coloring & Nature Journal SeriesBy Pearl & Fawn
Explore the birds of Colorado—from the foothills to the forests, right from your own backyard.
This beautifully designed coloring and journaling book features 30 iconic birds found throughout the Centennial State, from the bold Rufous Hummingbird to the curious Black-billed Magpie. Whether you're a beginner or a seasoned birder, this interactive book invites you to learn, color, and record your birdwatching adventures across Colorado.
Bring this book alongside your favorite bird field guide—use the guide for identifying species, then use this book to reflect on the moment, log your sightings, and color each bird in your own creative way.
Each bird is presented across two thoughtfully formatted pages:🖼️ Page 1: A full-color reference image with the bird’s name, space to record the date spotted, and a lined notes section for personal observations.🎨 Page 2: A matching black-and-white coloring page, featuring the same bird in the same pose, printed single-sided to prevent bleed-through.
Whether you’re watching birds in the Rockies, spotting visitors in your city park, or journaling from your porch, this book is a peaceful companion to deepen your connection with Colorado’s wild beauty.

A Naturalist’s Masterpiece: 46 Iconic Illustrations from the Legendary John James Audubon 
Iconic Avian Selection: Bring vibrant life to legendary species including the Great Blue Heron, Ruby-Throated Hummingbird, and Painted Bunting.

Kennedy, based on the iconic original plates of famous naturalist John James Audubon. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: What a wonderful adult coloring book of Audubon’s Birds!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this book for a friend who loves birds and I looked through it before giving it to her, enjoying each and every page!  Dover has been publishing these kinds of books for many years, on a large number of topics, long before the recent adult coloring book revolution, and I bet you can find some on your bookshelf that you bought years ago!  The prices for these are very reasonable, too, often $3.99 or less, and this one is just $3.35 with free 2-day shipping if you have Amazon prime!  The only drawback for these books is that they are printed back-to-back so if you use markers they bleed through and ruin the picture on the other side.  However the detailed drawings really call for colored pencils where you can do shading, and this book is perfect for that!  Or, you can copy the page you want to color on good quality copy paper of the weight you prefer (I like the Hammerhill color copy cover paper, 60 lb. weight, which is like a very light cardboard like you would use as a cover to a report).  This is a wonderful book for anyone who likes birds and I highly recommend it!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got many of these books in different themes and love coloring them. You can get really creative. I don't have an artist's talent, so I enjoy creating my own color combinations, although there are colored pictures of all of them on the covers so you can follow those or come up with your own. These aren't not kids coloring books! They are more detailed, and I use colored pencils on some, fine point gel pens on others and a wide range of felt tip colors on most. I usually do these in the evening when I need to wind down and they work wonders for me. Even without artistic talent,  I love my renderings and plan on keeping the completed books to look at a few years from now or give some of them to an elderly friend who loves them when I finish coloring them. Great idea for adults or kids who have advanced coloring skills.
